changes.historical_text: This card can only be activated when any player has 6 or more cards on the field and/or in their hand. The player(s) then select and send cards to their respective Graveyards until the amount remaining on the field and in their hand is 5.
changes.summary: No implementation-relevant difference is attested: the goat entry's cdb text is byte-identical to the pinned modern text (both lineage v2, DB2-EN199), and the single behaviour upstream annotates — "Cannot send itself" — is implemented by the modern script too, which passes `local exc=c:IsRelateToEffect(e) and c or nil` as the selection exception for the activating player (the opponent only ever picks from their own cards). What remains in the diff is unattested implementation idiom: the goat script merges both players' picks into one group sent with REASON_EFFECT, while the modern script sends each player's picks in a separate call with REASON_RULE; 0xe and LOCATION_ONFIELD|LOCATION_HAND are the same locations.

review.notes: Escalation reason: the residual script difference IS observable — REASON_EFFECT vs REASON_RULE decides whether the sent cards count as sent by a card effect, and one merged send vs two sequential sends decides whether both players' sent-to-Graveyard triggers (Sangan/Witch-style) enter one SEGOC chain or two — but no upstream annotation, ruling source or text supports either side as the era behaviour, and upstream's own stated reason for the variant is already satisfied by the modern script. I recorded the honest cosmetic verdict and flagged it rather than inventing an era ruling. Lineage v0 (LOD-090, 2003-06-06) -> v1 -> v2 are all cosmetic and v0/v1 predate the baseline version.
